rubric_notes: Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22. Correctly states SCOPe 2.08 class a, fold a.22, single superfamily a.22.1 and all four curated families (a.22.1.1-a.22.1.4) plus the a.22.1.0 automated-matches node, all supported by the evidence bundle. Identifies the superfamily as the level supporting a probable evolutionary relationship, insists family distinctions be preserved, and explicitly rejects annotating TAF/bacterial domains as nucleosome histones or transferring DNA-packing function wholesale. No fabricated identifiers or annotations; no material omission.

Correct families a.204.1.2 and a.204.1.4, shared superfamily a.204.1, boundaries match bundle. Frames the relationship as stronger than fold-only but weaker than same-family, and rejects transfer of PRA-PH activity, histidine-biosynthesis role, substrate specificity, or relabeling. Evaluator: claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-22.

Correct family SCCS under superfamily c.55.1, fold c.55, class c, supported by the fold and superfamily children listings in the bundle. Identifies the superfamily assignment as the remote-homology statement, permits only broad structural/mechanistic expectations for the ATP-binding core and remote templates, and explicitly excludes family-level substrate specificity, full function, regulatory behavior, quaternary state and boundaries; correctly notes fold-level similarity to other c.55 superfamilies is not homology evidence. Complete.

Correct hierarchy and SUNIDs; bimetal-centre superfamily comment supported. Representative domains d1aewa_, d1afra_, d1jkua_ exist in bundle with lineages confirming a.25.1 as lowest shared node (the 'same_superfamily' pairwise phrasing is not from a comparison endpoint but is derivable from the parents responses; d1afra_ correctly described as a diiron a.25.1.2 member). Interprets as common ancestry followed by family-specific divergence, explicitly rejects ferritin/catalase transfer across families, and notes fold a.25 is weaker than a.25.1 (other superfamilies correctly cited). Evidence requirement named (active-site, metal-binding, substrate, quaternary). Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct families b.6.1.1, b.6.1.5, b.6.1.6 under superfamily b.6.1 and fold b.6, supported by bundle. Refuses copper/electron-transfer transfer and requires metal-ligating residues and biochemical role to be independently supported; no unsafe transfer. Omission: never states explicitly that superfamily membership implies probable common ancestry, and the phrase 'implied by the shared superfamily/fold' blurs the superfamily-versus-fold homology distinction central to the question. Evaluator: claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-22.

Correct lineage and family SCCS; correctly notes SCOPe treats superfamily but not fold as homology-implying, matching the d.15 homology endpoint warning in the bundle. Infers remote common ancestry and shared beta-grasp scaffold, and rejects transferring ubiquitin identity, covalent modifier/E1-E2-E3 conjugation, Ras-GTPase binding, and p97/VCP-adaptor UBX behavior across d.15.1.1/d.15.1.2/d.15.1.5. Clearly states limits of what the superfamily supports. All criteria met. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

Correct families under CheY-like c.23.1 (SUNID 52172), fold c.23, class c; family lists and KaiA annotation supported by bundle. Distinguishes superfamily-level homology from mere shared fold and rejects canonical receiver status for ODC wing/KaiA and PLP decarboxylase transfer to CheY/KaiA; cautions against transferring active-site residues, phosphorylation/Mg2+ chemistry, substrate specificity, quaternary state. Omits explicit rejection of circadian-regulation transfer; AlphaFold/representative remark is extraneous. No must_avoid violations. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22. Correct lineage with SUNIDs 310577/310616, d3ikja2 boundaries and P. horikoshii OT3 A1 protein verified, fold comment, all sibling superfamilies named. Correctly explains that SCOPe does not treat b.84 as one homologous unit, homology inferred within b.84.5, fold sharing says only comparable fold, and refuses function/template transfer to b.84.1-b.84.4; correctly scopes PubMed 19893485 as support for the grouping, not for fold-wide homology. Calling d3ikja2 'the representative domain returned for that family' reflects an odd sccs resolution to a species node but is not a fabrication.

Correct 2.08 fold f.21/81344 and superfamilies f.21.1/81342, f.21.2/81343, f.21.3/103501 with correct family-level members (supported by children responses); correctly notes homology implied per superfamily, not at the fold parent. Rejects merging and cross-group transfer without asserting absolute non-homology. Only says 'unless other evidence is supplied' and never specifies the sequence, structural-detail, motif, and biological-context evidence required. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

Correct identifiers throughout; Pfam PF02254 mapping and the c.2.1.1 'N-terminal all-beta domain defines family' comment are both supported by the annotations evidence. Attributes the remote evolutionary relationship to superfamily membership, separates it from family-level closeness, and refuses to transfer substrate chemistry, CoA binding, K-channel/RCK regulation, NAD vs NADP preference, domain boundaries or oligomeric context. The phrase 'superfamily/fold depth' is slightly loose but the homology claim is correctly anchored at the superfamily. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Complete. Correct shared lineage, explicit family SUNID 100905 with the 'not a true family' annotation, correct reading of the node as a grouping of designed trimeric coiled-coil constructs rather than evidence of true homology, and explicit refusal to transfer homology/function/template assumptions. Evaluator: claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-22.

Evaluator Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22. Correct 1.69 placement (d1t1ja_ in own fold/superfamily/family c.137/c.137.1/c.137.1.1 vs d1f8ya_ c.23.14.1, shared only class c). Correct 2.08 placement (d1t1ja1 A:1-118 c.23.14.2 vs d1f8ya_ c.23.14.1, shared superfamily c.23.14 N-(deoxy)ribosyltransferase-like). Interprets change as remote homology at superfamily level without family-level or activity transfer. All identifiers supported by the bundle. Minor: attributes the reclassification to 'Andreeva et al.' rather than SCOP curators as described by that paper; not material.

Identifies d1a14h2 as H:1-8 synthetic N-terminal tag in class l, l.1.1.1 (full lineage, Synthetic species); d1a14h1 as H:9-111 b.1.1.1 VH domain; explicitly rejects tag similarity as homology evidence and bars transfer to family/superfamily/fold/function/template. Homology warning claim supported by bundle. All must_include met, no must_avoid violations. Evaluator: claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-22.

Correct 1.75 lineage f.11.1.1 and correct 2.08 placements with boundaries A:14-225 b.179.1.1 PA14 and A:226-735 f.60.1.1, plus an explicit statement that the split does not make the two modules mutually homologous and that class, family, and toxin annotation must not cross the boundary. Does not identify 2.04 as the release where the split was introduced, giving only the 2.08 endpoint of the before/after comparison.

Correct five-domain inventory with full lineages; d3jb9a5 d.394 as newly observed fold; four reused modules; stepwise-accretion inference hedged with superfamily-level caveat and no function/template transfer. Chain-hit bundle confirms 3jb9A is its own representative (the '90 percent' threshold wording is an unsupported but immaterial detail). Evaluator: Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct hierarchy and protein/species placements; frames family as repeat-family homology statement rather than fixed-length domain; cites re heterogeneity, single-repeat comment, representative repeat 4cj9 A:259-292; lists unsafe transfers (repeat count, boundaries, RVD specificity, function). Statement that 3v6pA is not its own cluster representative is supported by the chain hits bundle.

Correct bundle-supported metadata (2.08 / 2.08-stable, periodic 2.08-2026-08-16) and correct advice to pin the stable release; properly says the periodic label is not a new independent release. Does not address preserving the dated label when periodic-only entries are used, and gives no explanation that periodic updates add newly classified PDB entries without rewriting older stable-release domains. Evaluator: claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-22.

Correct placement of all fragment SIDs and d1dn1b_ in a.47.2.1, protein node for the curated rat entries, ms caveat, automated-match branch to d3c98b_. Treats the fragment assignments as partial observations of the family fold, refuses to transfer boundaries, domain count, or t-SNARE function from a three-helix match, distinguishes family-level homology evidence from fold-only similarity at a.47, and recommends the full d3c98b_ chain as representative. Spectrin resolution is implicit rather than stated, but the inference and limits are complete. Evaluator: claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-22.

Correctly names folds c.2, c.3, c.25, c.31 and their superfamilies with accurate descriptions, and notes they share only class c. Makes the level-dependent inference, treats cross-fold NAD(P) binding as convergent with respect to the cofactor phenotype 'unless there is stronger evidence', explains recurring physical constraints on dinucleotide pockets and catalytic constellations, and requires global structural correspondence, sequence/profile support, and full catalytic context before merging, transferring EC function, or choosing templates. No bundle, but all classifications stated are correct. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

Classifications and releases are right: 2.04 ColG at b.23.2.1 in CUB-like fold b.23 versus Cry3A d1dlca1 (A:500-644) at b.18.1.3, and 2.08 ColG at b.18.1.36 with chain B resolved as d1nqdb1 plus a two-residue l.1.1.1 fragment, Cry3A unchanged. Conclusion is correctly pitched at superfamily-strength remote homology with different families and no boundary or function copying. Supporting evidence for ancestry is weak, resting on the reclassification itself and a generic statement that both are all-beta terminal ligand-binding modules, without alignment or literature support. Eval: Fable 5.1, 2026-10-22.

Correct lineage and SUNID 46690; homology justified at family level and explicitly distinguished from fold-only resemblance; hf defined correctly; rejects coordinate transfer, fold-specific template modeling, and automatic functional-site transfer; recommends excluding or downweighting d1ztra1 in representative sets/ML splits that assume one fold per family member. Adds supported mutant/NHE-complex caveats and asks for external structural/biochemical evidence. Evaluator: Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1), 2026-10-22.

Correct release, family SUNID 49266, boundaries, protein nodes, and fr definition, supported by bundle. Family homology preserved; align only over contained core without inferring absent strands/boundaries from d1uc6a1; prefer d1uc6a1 or another non-fragment domain, use fragment only when explicitly acceptable; truncated entry must not exaggerate diversity; rejects receptor/ligand function and template transfer. Quality of the complete candidate not discussed but recommendation hedged. Evaluator claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-22.

Complete. Correct choice; class/fold/superfamily/family semantics stated accurately with correct 2.08 examples (a, a.4 DNA/RNA-binding 3-helical bundle, a.4.1 Homeodomain-like). Explicitly says lack of superfamily-level homology alone does not justify a new fold, which addresses the must_avoid criterion directly. Notes folds may contain nonhomologous superfamilies, rejects transfer of ancestry/function/templates, and lists evidence needed for a common-ancestry hypothesis. Evaluator: claude-fable-5-1, 2026-10-22.

Uses exemplar domains d1atpe_ (d.144.1.7, mouse PKA), d1j7ua_ (d.144.1.6, E. faecalis APH IIIa), d1e8xa4 (d.144.1.4, pig PI3Kgamma A:726-1092); lineages in the bundle confirm their lowest common node is superfamily d.144.1. Family SCCS and names correct. Concludes probable common ancestry of the catalytic core and restricts safe transfer to the PK-like ATP-dependent core; names substrate specificity, activation-loop behavior, regulatory subunits, and inhibitor selectivity as unsafe. Lists profiles/HMMs, structures of the pocket, catalytic-residue conservation, ligand/mutagenesis data, and biochemical assays. Adds a supported domain-boundary caveat for 1e8x multi-domain chain. Complete.
